officialTitle: Sotorasib versus docetaxel for previously treated non-small-cell lung cancer with KRAS G12C mutation: a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial
subtypes: Previously treated with platinum chemotherapy and PD-(L)1 inhibitor

design.blinding: Open-label; PFS by blinded independent central review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between June 4, 2020, and April 26, 2021, 345 patients were randomly assigned to receive sotorasib (n=171 [50%]) or docetaxel (n=174 [50%]).
design.notes: Stratified by prior lines, ethnicity and history of CNS metastases.

clinicalQuestion: In previously treated KRAS G12C-mutant advanced NSCLC, does sotorasib improve PFS over docetaxel?

pico.population: KRAS G12C-mutant advanced NSCLC progressing after platinum chemotherapy and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor

publications.title: Sotorasib versus docetaxel for previously treated non-small-cell lung cancer with KRASmutation: a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.endpointLabel: PFS by blinded independent central review
outcomes.sourceQuote: After a median follow-up of 17·7 months (IQR 16·4-20·1), the study met its primary endpoint of a statistically significant increase in the progression-free survival for sotorasib, compared with docetaxel (median progression-free survival 5·6 months [95% CI 4·3-7·8] vs 4·5 months [3·0-5·7]; hazard ratio 0·66 [0·51-0·86]; p=0·0017).

safety.description: Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events; serious treatment-related adverse events
safety.sourceQuote: Sotorasib was well tolerated, with fewer grade 3 or worse (n=56 [33%] vs n=61 [40%]) and serious treatment-related adverse events compared with docetaxel (n=18 [11%] vs n=34 [23%]).

safety.description: Most common grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events with sotorasib
safety.sourceQuote: For sotorasib, the most common treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were diarrhoea (n= 20 [12%]), alanine aminotransferase increase (n=13 [8%]), and aspartate aminotransferase increase (n=9 [5%]).

strengths: First randomised phase III of a KRAS G12C inhibitor
limitations: OS not reported in the abstract

clinicalImplications.text: Confirmed a PFS advantage and more favourable tolerability for sotorasib over docetaxel in pretreated KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Watch for diarrhoea and transaminase elevations on sotorasib, particularly soon after prior immunotherapy.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 36764316. Abstract text strips the 'G12C' superscript; mutation identity taken from trial context.
